title: GitHub Actions concurrency policy (.github/policy.rego): the missing-concurrency denial must not suggest the github.ref group; opt-out is a run_id group with cancel-in-progress false
answers: Conftest says my workflow must declare 'concurrency' explicitly, what should I write?
Why does the policy suggest a github.run_id concurrency group instead of github.ref?
Which workflow triggers are unsafe with a github.ref-based concurrency group?
Where is the denial message for a workflow missing concurrency generated?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_workflow_without_concurrency returns the Conftest denial for a workflow YAML under .github/workflows that does not declare a `concurrency` key, and the text of that message is the guidance an author reads when fixing it.
Rule: The message must not recommend the canned group '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}', which is unsafe for pull_request_target, issue_comment, issues and workflow_run. The only opt-out it offers is a complete block: `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which places each run in its own group.
Symptom: Following the old ref-based group guidance contributed to the release-note.yml cancellation bug, where runs cancelled each other (fixed in #25624).
Constraints: A unique per-run group only stops concurrency-based cancellation and serialization. It does not promise that a run completes, since runner-capacity queuing or cancellation from other causes still apply, so the message is worded as "allow each run to proceed independently" for concurrency grouping. This changes message text only, not the detection logic that requires the key.
applies: Workflow YAML under .github/workflows checked by Conftest with .github/policy.rego; covers the wording of the missing-concurrency message, not when the key is required.
says: Conftest says my workflow must declare concurrency, but the suggested group is unsafe for my triggers
The missing-concurrency error tells me to use a ref-based group that made my release runs cancel each other
What concurrency setting should I write to stop Conftest from rejecting my workflow without a concurrency block?
Why does the workflow policy push a per-run concurrency group instead of a branch-based one?
search: GitHub Actions missing-concurrency policy denial message wording: the message must not recommend the ref-based concurrency group and offers a per-run group with cancel-in-progress false as the only opt-out. Detection requiring the concurrency key is unchanged.
